nodes.label: G-2 throughput gate — deferred to a 4-vCPU cloud run
nodes.rationale: First check on that run is iperf3 -u -b 0's Lost/Total datagrams, not Mbit/s: if the ~98% receive-side loss reproduces on real hardware the bottleneck is boringtun's receive pipeline rather than the environment, and Bet 1's throughput claim is at risk.

nodes.label: Measured boringtun tunnel throughput (~7.5-7.8 Mbit/s, container)
bpffs mounts don't cross ip netns exec — map-id file workaround
nodes.rationale: BPF object IDs are system-global, so the enforcer writes a pin-dir-keyed map-id file to /tmp (which survives the unshares) and re-verifies the map name via MapInfo. Known limitation: name re-verification cannot detect id reuse by a same-named map from another instance.

nodes.label: nft one-line ruleset with '; } }' does not parse
udpshim peer-learning chicken/egg
nodes.rationale: The downlink can only deliver to whichever local address last sent, so a one-sided ping would have its handshake initiation silently dropped at the peer's shim; the test primes both sides with concurrent background pings. A design property, not a bug.

nodes.label: masquerade fully-random genuinely maps per-destination
nodes.rationale: The flagged risk that kernel SNAT port-preservation would defeat fully-random did not materialise on kernel 6.12.76-linuxkit, so no explicit per-destination snat range fallback was needed.
